intro.sing: The piano plays a note. Then the microphone opens and you sing the note back, on any vowel or a hum. Five notes, one at a time.
intro.tuner: Sing or hum any note. The page shows which note it is and how far you're from its center, in cents.
intro.ear: Two piano notes play, one after the other. Was the second one higher or lower? Three pairs, and the microphone stays off.

sing.now: Now sing it back, and hold it.
sing.notHeard: Not heard, so this note doesn't count.

result.label: Typical miss
result.offSay: Half your notes sat further than {cents} from the piano, half closer.
result.wobbleSay: Once you arrived on a note, it moved about {cents} while you held it.
result.wobbleRead: Under about 10 cents is a steady hold. Vibrato reads higher, and that's part of the sound, not a mistake.
result.wobbleNone: The notes were too short to see whether they moved while you held them.
result.cent: 100 cents make a semitone, one piano key to the next.
result.sample: Five notes is a small sample. Another round will move these numbers a little.
result.tooFew: The microphone heard {judged} of {total} notes clearly, which is too few to measure. Try again a little louder or closer to the microphone. Humming works too.
result.ctaBody: Scalita's Accuracy Training goes further: match any note on a live pitch trail, or sing back leaps from songs, in your own range. Free on Android, no account.

ear.label: Higher or lower
ear.question: Was the second note higher or lower?
ear.wentUp: The second note was higher, {step} up.
ear.wentDown: The second note was lower, {step} down.
ear.score: You heard the direction of {right} of {total} pairs.
ear.all: That held down to one semitone, the smallest step on a piano.
ear.some: The smallest steps are the hardest to hear at first. Headphones and a quiet room help.

pianoFailed: The piano didn't load. Check your connection and try again.
